items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I didn't know any of Horace's musicians well, but I talked with some of them the same as I had done with other musicians that I didn't know very well.

ctx.x: The next time that Fletcher came to Cincy was the day before Helvey was to go to Lexington to play the fair. There was a dance at the Crystal Ballroom this Sunday afternoon with the Horace Henderson orchestra from Wilberforce College and Fletcher was such a big drawing attraction that Zack White was having him at the Armory, which was the biggest place in town to give a dance.

I was at the Crystal and Horace's boys with Freddie Jenkins, Joe and Casper McCord and Red Hicks on trombone were sounding real great. Fletcher gave Horace quite a few of his arrangemnts and Horace came close to playing them almost like Fletcher. There was a little fat brown-skin guy that was standing against the wall near the band stand who looked like he was mad at the world and only smiled occasionally when one of the musicians in the band looked his way.

I didn't know any of Horace's musicians well, but I talked with some of them the same as I had done with other musicians that I didn't know very well. So I asked one of the musicians at the intermission who the little fat salty looking guy was, and he told me that he was Rex Steward, a trumpet player that had taken Joe Smith's place in Fletcher's band.
